text:
Kyle Connor has 18 goals in 23 games, and our wins added, which credits goals at the moments they swing games, puts him second among 548 skaters. TSN had Bruce Boudreau explaining "why it's so hard to stop Kyle Connor," and the tracking data gives a clue: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 66% of his entries last season, and in the 87th percentile among forwards for chances from the home-plate area in front of the net.

The shooting volume is real. His 98 shots and 13.4 expected goals (the quality of his chances) are both up sharply on last season's rate, and Winnipeg's 5v5 chance share is 7.3 points better with him than without.

The finishing is the part to watch. He is shooting 18.4%, against 14% last season and above the top of our range for him, so 18 goals on 13.4 expected is a pace that usually cools even when the chances hold. Evolving-Hockey had him 34th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement last season. Our range for his season is 42 to 60 goals and 83 to 110 points.
